name: ShaderGradient
one_liner: Customizable 3D animated WebGL gradients for Figma, Framer and React, with a free web editor.
what_it_offers: A browser editor (shadergradient.co/customize) where you set shape (plane, sphere or waterPlane), colors, noise, lighting, grain, camera and animation. Every setting is saved in a shareable URL query string. You can use the same gradient through the MIT-licensed React package @shadergradient/react (built on three.js and react-three-fiber), a Framer plugin/component, or a Figma plugin (62.7k users, also works in FigJam, Slides and Buzz) that makes snapshots, adds GIFs to the canvas, and exports looping .gif/.webm files.
tech_stack: React + three.js + @react-three/fiber (WebGL shaders); marketing site built on Framer
portfolio_fit_reason: A fast route to a signature animated hero or section background on a React/Next or Framer portfolio, with a visual editor and typed component. It covers one effect only, and the look is common unless carefully art-directed.
client_ok_note: Code is MIT per README and npm metadata (repo lacks a LICENSE file). Framer plugin license listed as 'Limited'; exported GIF/WebM assets have no explicit terms.
best_use_for_portfolio: Design a slow, brand-colored gradient in the /customize editor and render it behind the name and intro line of your portfolio home page via the urlString prop, lazy-loaded with a pixelDensity cap. Export a WebM or still as the reduced-motion and low-power fallback, and reuse the same palette as a subtle backdrop on case-study headers.
tier_reason: A quick path to a live animated gradient hero in React, Next.js or Framer, with a visual editor. It offers one effect, and the look is common without art direction.
pick_over_overlaps: Use it when you want a live, configurable animated gradient shipped as a React component. Push the settings well off the presets.
score_rationale: One of the quickest ways to get a distinctive, high-quality animated hero background into a React/Next site: design it visually, then drop in a typed component. It only does one visual effect, not whole layouts, and the look is widely used, so it needs careful art direction to stay distinctive.
free_tier: Free: the web editor, the React npm package (MIT), the Framer plugin (no price listed on the Marketplace), and Figma static snapshots. In the Figma plugin, GIF/video extraction (adding a GIF or video to the canvas, or downloading .gif/.webm) has a free trial. After it ends, the plugin shows 'Upgrade to Pro'. The plugin source sets the trial to 7 days (`const trials = 7`, counted from trial_started_at, with a '(N days left)' label). I could not open the plugin inside Figma to see that screen.
paid_entry_label: Figma plugin Pro $4/mo billed monthly, or $24/yr billed yearly (about $2/mo). Confirmed on the live Stripe checkout pages 'Subscribe to Shadergradient' ($4.00 per month; $24.00 per year, billed annually, plus tax) that the plugin's upgrade button opens.
paid_top_label: Figma plugin Pro yearly $24/yr (about $2/mo), the only paid tier
commercial_use_license: The code is MIT (© ruucm, stone-skipper), as stated in the README and in the npm package metadata, so you can use it on commercial sites. The GitHub repo has no LICENSE file (the API's /license endpoint returns 404). The Framer Marketplace lists the plugin license as 'Limited', linking to Framer's community terms. No explicit license terms were found for exported GIF/video assets.
agent_friendly: npm package @shadergradient/react with typed props. An agent can paste a /customize URL into the urlString prop (control='query') to reproduce a designed gradient exactly. The README has CodeSandbox starters for CRA, Next.js (Pages and App Router) and Vite + React 19, plus a compatibility table. No MCP server, shadcn registry or llms.txt (shadergradient.co/llms.txt returns 404).
maintenance_signal: GitHub ruucm/shadergradient: 2,438 stars, last push 2026-09-04. The last main-branch commit is v2.4.24 on 2026-06-11. The npm latest tag is still 2.4.20 (published 2025-12-08) and got 19,047 downloads in the week of Sept 5-11, 2026. The plugin's pricing and trial code was last changed 2025-12-11. Figma plugin Version 10 (FigJam support) came out on 2025-12-16.
caveats: Adds three.js and R3F to the bundle, which is heavy for a background, and needs a GPU with WebGL. The Next 15 App Router requires React 19 + R3F v9 (per the README). The npm release lags the repo (2.4.20 vs 2.4.24). Figma Pro is billed through external Stripe links, not Figma's built-in payments, so you cancel through the plugin's 'support' link (Stripe customer portal), not in Figma account settings; one Figma comment reports confusion about this. The 7-day trial length comes from plugin source code, not from the in-Figma screen. Some Figma comments report short or failed WebM exports and low-res snapshots. The popular 'Stripe-like gradient' look can feel generic.
unverified_fields: free_tier (7-day trial length taken from plugin source code; the in-Figma upgrade/trial screen was not opened, since that needs a Figma login)
